content: If you have any questions about how to store this medication, consult your pharmacist. Do not freeze the product. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last updated in May 2024. This document is a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Rarely, serious kidney problems have been reported with the use of this product. Conditions such as heart failure, kidney disease, bowel problems (e.g., blockage, ulcerative colitis), or being over the age of 55 may increase the risk. Taking certain medications that affect kidney function (refer to the Drug Interactions section) can also elevate the risk. This medication may be used to relieve occasional constipation. However, for constipation, it is generally recommended to use milder products, such as stool softeners or bulk-forming laxatives, whenever possible. Discuss alternative treatment options with your doctor or pharmacist. Your doctor may also prescribe this product, often in combination with other products, to cleanse the intestines before surgery or certain bowel procedures (e.g., colonoscopy, radiography). Sodium phosphate is a saline laxative that is believed to work by increasing fluid in the small intestine. Follow all instructions on the product packaging carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. To improve the taste, this product may be chilled in the refrigerator before use, but do not freeze it. Mix your dose in 8 ounces (240 milliliters) of liquid and drink the solution. If your doctor has instructed you to use this product before surgery or a bowel procedure, they will provide specific timing instructions. Follow your doctor’s directions closely. After taking the medication, drink plenty of clear fluids as directed by your doctor to help prevent serious side effects such as kidney problems or dehydration. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, procedure, age, and response to treatment. Do not take more of this medication than directed, use it more than once in 24 hours, or use it for more than three days unless instructed by your doctor. Additionally, do not use other laxative products while using this medication unless directed by your doctor. Prolonged or frequent use of this medication may lead to a condition known as laxative dependence, which can result in ongoing constipation and loss of normal bowel function. For most individuals with occasional constipation, a bulk-forming laxative (e.g., psyllium) or a stool softener (e.g., docusate) is a safer and more effective option. Mild side effects such as abdominal discomfort, cramps, gas, or nausea may occur. If your doctor has directed you to use this product, remember that they have determined the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent diarrhea may lead to dehydration, which can cause serious complications for the kidneys and heart. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using sodium phosphate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Consult your doctor before using this product if you have experienced a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks or if you need to use a laxative daily for more than one week. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The watery bowel movements caused by sodium phosphate may reduce the absorption and effectiveness of your regular medications. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function, blood mineral levels) may be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. For storage, refer to the instructions on the package label. If you have any questions about storage, consult your pharmacist. Do not freeze the product or store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
